children: Complan, the nutrition drink brand from Zydus Wellness, has launched its latest campaign, ‘India ka Complan Boy’, featuring brand ambassador and young Indian cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The campaign aims to refresh Complan’s long-standing ‘Complan Boy’ brand equity for a new generation of families, drawing on Sooryavanshi’s journey of ambition, discipline and preparation.

The campaign builds on Complan’s association with children who dream big and the families who support those aspirations. It brings the brand’s iconic advertising character into a contemporary context through the story of Sooryavanshi, positioning him as a representation of the new-age ‘India ka Complan Boy’.

At 15, Sooryavanshi became the youngest cricketer to debut for India in international cricket, surpassing Sachin Tendulkar’s record. He has also continued to make his mark internationally, including scoring his maiden T20 half-century against Zimbabwe in July.

Speaking about the campaign, Tarun Arora, CEO and Whole-Time Director, Zydus Wellness, said, “Brands stay relevant when they continue to evolve with the people they serve. At Complan, we have a distinctive legacy of celebrating children who dream big, and today’s generation is dreaming in new and different ways.

Vaibhav represents that evolution beautifully. His journey is a story of ambition, preparation, perseverance, and family support. These values have always been at the heart of Complan. With ‘India ka Complan Boy’ we are refreshing a much-loved brand equity and bringing it into the lives of a new generation in a way that feels authentic to them.”
The campaign is anchored in Complan’s ‘Thoda Plan, Thoda Complan’ philosophy, highlighting preparation, discipline, family support and nutrition as factors behind achieving long-term goals.

For Sooryavanshi, the association has personal significance. “Playing in the IPL and getting the opportunity to represent India at such a young age is something I feel very grateful for. I know I still have a long way to go and a lot to learn. Whatever I have achieved so far has only been possible because of the support of my family, coaches, and teammates. We are three brothers who have grown up with Complan in the house, so becoming ‘India ka Complan Boy’ feels really special. I hope it encourages other children to dream big, work hard, and always remain grounded,” he said.
The campaign is supported by a digital film tracing key moments from Sooryavanshi’s journey, from preparation and training to the milestones that have shaped his rise in Indian cricket.
